To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
teleological actions are needed to assess and handle critical incidents that cause emotional responses in service encounters.

critical incidents are not only a matter of negative emotional responses but also of teleological actions, interactive interfaces and perceptual gaps, which are the three categories of critical incidents that we have defined and described.

(1) the service encounter is an interactive interface between a service provider and a service recipient; (2) a critical incident is an unexpected, unanticipated or unpredictable event that is experienced by a service recipient as a deviation from the service recipient’s expectation, and (3) a perceptual gap is a difference between a service provider’s understanding of an incident and a service recipient’s understanding of the incident.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the teleological actions of service providers and customers in service encounters that are perceived to be critical incidents.
the study of teleology, the study of critical incidents in service interactions and the management of negative emotions.
the assessment of negative emotions in service encounter critical incidents.
